All three blockers were one mechanical class: **an edit that replaces a workflow-surface literal
which a `tests/` file pins.** The v4 edit-spec had not grepped for those pins. Both fixes are
REDESIGNS of the edit, not adaptations of the tests — the round now removes no pinned literal at
all, so it edits zero pin-test files.

1. `ensemble-cap-pin-collision` (BLOCKER, addressed) — v4's E3 rewrote the 1b launcher's
   `uv run pytest <files>` to `$S9C_FILES`, but `tests/test_ensemble_review_cap.py:206-207`
   requires that literal on the same non-backtick span as the rc-write, and v4's E10 pinned its
   ABSENCE — jointly unsatisfiable. **v5:** the launcher line is byte-identical; the refusal
   became a CROSS-CHECK of the substituted set's path count against the selector's live count.
   Measured (`artifacts/probe-gateset-crosscheck.txt`): refuses on empty, whitespace-only,
   tabs+newline, the unsubstituted literal `<files>`, and a short 3-path stale copy; launches
   only on the exact count. Strictly stronger than v4's emptiness-only refusal — it also catches
   a stale or short copy, which is the shape a wrong `--json` key actually produces.
2. `guard3-verdict-literal-locators` (BLOCKER, addressed) — v4's E7 one-read rewrite deleted three
   strings pinned in `tests/test_step10d_guard3.py`: `_SHA_CHECK` (641-644),
   `_NONEMPTY_SHA_CHECK` (645), and the verdict-probe string at 667/699 — the last used as a
   region LOCATOR, so its disappearance breaks the tests before any assert runs. That file is
   WORKFLOW_INVARIANT (manifest line 90): a wrong adaptation reds every session's gate
   fleet-wide. **v5:** E7 is additive comment prose only — the #2006 re-compose ban, which IS the
   filed D4 defect (the improvised process-substitution compare exists in neither surface, so
   what was missing was the instruction not to re-compose it), plus a note that the grep scans the
   whole file, which is why the never-hand-write rule is load-bearing there. The one-read form is
   deferred with its pin-adaptation cost recorded.
3. `files-only-newline-splice` (BLOCKER, addressed) — `--files-only` emits one path per line and
   `$( )` preserves interior newlines, so v4's splice would have inserted real command separators
   into the launcher's inner single-quoted script: pytest on the first file only, no `--junitxml`.
   **v5:** moot — the per-line output is consumed only by a line count, never spliced.
